data.revised_prompt: The spatial layout of the four red dots and two intersecting blue lines forming an X-shape in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The target image is a photorealistic, top-down industrial design rendering of a cold grey quadcopter replacing the diagram from <Picture 1>, with its motor positions and arm directions guided by <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> serves as a weak reference for the quadcopter's spatial geometry; the four red dot positions guide the placement of the four motors at a 30cm rotor-to-rotor distance, while the blue line trajectories guide the stretched X-shaped foldable arms with a 0.7:1 arm span ratio and a 35° rotor angle, without rendering the literal dots or lines. Viewed from a direct 90-degree overhead perspective against a clean studio surface, the drone features a streamlined central fuselage with a 60-degree edge angle, matte carbon fiber framing, and anodized aluminum honeycomb grilles. A discreet GPS antenna module sits on the top center surface, and a glowing blue LED light band runs along the fuselage perimeter. Four foldable arms extend outward via modular quick-release connectors toward the four corners defined by <Subject 1>, each tipped with reinforced motor covers and translucent ABS propellers featuring a glossy nano-coating. Soft 5500K studio lighting illuminates the airframe, casting crisp, high-contrast shadows directly beneath the fuselage, arms, and spinning rotors.
